items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: And so I met Mr. Keegan or Hogan or -- and I asked him if he could open a door for me on television.

ctx.x: So I was beginning to get these club dates. And between that and the teaching, -- it wasn't great, but we were beginning to get by, without working -- where I was going to get pushed out of work. And pretty soon, the Showboat Sahara, -- the Sorry S, or as the musicians called it, the Sorry Ass, got to be the last one I worked, just about. And of course, along about this time, I did an article for the Daily News,

'Tell It Like It Is.' And so I met Mr. Keegan or Hogan or -- and I asked him if he could open a door for me on television. See, I tried radio and Studs tried for me, but for me to do a program on radio, no, there's no place for me, unless you go out and get a sponsor.

So I couldn't do that, so I had to give up. I'm not capable of getting sponsors. So I tried to break the door down, and he says, well, maybe I could do something for you on Channel 11, WTTW. It was on on the South Side at that time. I went out there, and I auditioned. I played along and told the story of jazz as I knew it.
